This is the one thing this skill exists for, and it is the one thing three
isolated baseline runs did not do (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-morpheus.txt`).
All three executed a four-stage plan end to end and left no on-disk record of
progress until the very last write — one left none at all. A session ending
anywhere before that leaves a working tree full of unattributed diff and no way
to tell which stages produced it, which were finished, or what was still
running.

Reading a mid-run tree is **not** this skill's problem. The companion baseline
(`scenario-relay-morpheus-resume.txt`) shows a fresh session doing that correctly
unprompted, against pressure to trust stale checkboxes. Relay adds nothing
there and says nothing about it.

**Violating the letter of this is violating the spirit of it.** "I'll record it
when the stage returns" is the failure, not a variation on it — the stages that
need recording most are the ones that never return.

## Handing a run to another session

Every run gets a short number when it is created, and `init` prints the
sentence that resumes it:

```
hand this to any session:  continue RUN-3
```

That sentence is the whole interface. A fresh session — another machine,
another host, a colleague — needs nothing else: **"continue RUN-3"**. It has no
transcript, so the ledger is what it reads, and the ledger is on disk because
it was written before the work, not after.

```sh
relay-morpheus.sh list          # every run, what is open, and its resume sentence
relay-morpheus.sh resume 3      # everything a session that has never seen it needs
relay-morpheus.sh 3 status      # any command takes the id first
```

`RUN-3`, `run-3` and `3` all resolve to the same run, because whoever types it
next is working from memory of a conversation rather than from a path. With one
run open and no id given, that run is assumed; with two or more, the script
refuses rather than guessing.

## The run file

`.skillator/run-<id>-<slug>.md`, one per run, in the repo. Markdown because a human and any
host both have to read it with no tooling. Git-tracked by default; a repo that
objects can `.gitignore` it and lose only the shared view, not the resume.

```markdown
# RUN-7 — notekeep v2
plan: docs/plans/PLAN-notekeep.md
started: 2026-09-22T09:14Z   updated: 2026-09-22T10:02Z

## Stages
| # | stage | state | owner | heartbeat | landed |
|---|-------|-------|-------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | list --json      | x | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T09:22Z | 3f1a2c9 |
| 2 | tags + --tag     | ~ | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T10:02Z | - |
| 3 | export           |   | -            | -     | - |
| 4 | README           |   | -            | -     | - |

## In flight
### stage 2 — tags + --tag  (dispatched 09:51)
prompt: |
  Add a `tags` list to each note in notekeep/store.py and a `list --tag <t>`
  filter in notekeep/cli.py. Test both. Do not touch export or the README.
last seen: wrote store.py, tests not yet run.

## Rulings
- 09:38 — stage 1 emits `[]` not `null` for an empty store — the plan does not
  say, JSON consumers expect a list — costs a one-line change if wrong.
```

**States:** `` (pending) · `~` in flight · `x` landed · `!` failed.
**`landed`** is a commit sha or a path, never a claim. An empty `landed` on an
`x` row is a lie the next session will believe.
**Rulings** are appended, never rewritten — see `tasks-sentinels`, which is
where they come from and which writes into this same file.

## The loop

1. **Before dispatch** — add or update the stage row to `~`, write the In-flight
   block with the *exact prompt you are about to send*, stamp the heartbeat.
   Prompt not written down → the agent is not recoverable → do not dispatch.
2. **While it runs** — re-stamp the heartbeat whenever the agent reports. A
   stale heartbeat is the only signal you get that a network drop took it;
   `hooks/relay-morpheus.* orphans` turns that into a list.
3. **When it lands** — commit the stage's work, then set `x` and put the sha in
   `landed`, and delete its In-flight block. In that order: the sha cannot be
   written before the commit exists.
4. **When it fails** — `!`, and leave the In-flight block where it is with the
   failure appended. A failed stage's prompt is the thing you need most.
5. **Never** delete a row. A run file only grows.

Stages that touch the same files do not run at once; independent ones do
(`PRACTICE.md` §4). Either way each gets its row before it gets its agent.

## Resuming

Open `.skillator/run.md`, then check it against the tree — the file is written
before the work, so the last `~` row is a stage that *started*, not one that
finished. `landed` shas are ground truth; anything else is a claim to verify.
Redispatch straight from the stored prompt; the rows are keyed by stage number,
so a redispatch that duplicates work overwrites rather than appends.

Then carry on. A resume does not need permission to continue — see
`grayskull-power` §3, **run to the end**.

## Scripts

`hooks/relay-morpheus.sh` · `hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1` — the same commands, mirrored per
`PLATFORMS.md`: `init`, `stage`, `heartbeat`, `status`, `orphans`. They are
bookkeeping, not judgement; every one reads or edits `.skillator/run.md` and
nothing else. Run `selftest` on both after touching either.

```sh
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  init plan.md "notekeep v2" "list --json" "tags" "export" "README"
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 2 '~' build:sonnet          # before you dispatch
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 2 x  build:sonnet 3f1a2c9   # after you commit
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  orphans 20                        # who has gone quiet
```

```powershell
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode init  -Plan plan.md -Title "notekeep v2" -Stages "list --json,tags,export,README"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 2 -State '~' -Owner build:sonnet
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 2 -State x   -Owner build:sonnet -Landed 3f1a2c9
```

Three constraints the pair has to keep, each learned the hard way:

- **Pure ASCII, and the empty cell is `-`, not an em dash.** Windows PowerShell
  5.1 reads a BOM-less script as ANSI and corrupts anything above 126.
- **The run file is LF with no BOM, written to a temp and moved.** Both mirrors
  edit the same file, so one of them flipping encoding rewrites every line in
  the diff; and a kill between truncate and write would empty the only record
  of what was in flight.
- **`-Stages` takes `"a,b,c"` and pending is spelled `pending`.** PowerShell's
  `-File` passes each argument as one literal string and drops empty ones, and
  `-File` is how every hook here invokes it.

### Seeing a run without being told about one

`list` prints every run with its resume sentence, and prints nothing when there
are none, so it is safe as a `SessionStart` hook. With one wired, a session that inherits
a half-finished run sees it in its own context before the user has to remember
to mention it — which is the difference between resuming and starting over.

```json
{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [ {
  "type": "command",
  "command": "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"<SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1\" -Mode list",
  "timeout": 5
} ] } ] } }
```

macOS/Linux: `sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh list`. Forward slashes throughout —
PowerShell accepts them and it removes all backslash-escaping from the JSON.
Other hosts have no equivalent event; there, reading `.skillator/run.md` is the
first thing `resume-cortana` does. `watch-cortana` already drains in-flight
agents at the limit — relay is what it drains *into*, so the two do not overlap.

# Task 3 report: export_markdown

**Status:** DONE

## 1. What was implemented
`notekeep/export.py`: `export_markdown(notes, path)` opens `path` for writing, writes one `- <text>\n` line per note, and returns `len(notes)`. Stdlib only, and it follows the `open(...) as fh` style used in `store.py`.

```python
def export_markdown(notes, path):
    with open(path, "w") as fh:
        for note in notes:
            fh.write("- " + note["text"] + "\n")
    return len(notes)

"""Notes on disk, one JSON file. Deliberately boring. No stage touches this."""
import json
import os

PATH = os.environ.get("NOTEKEEP_PATH", "notes.json")


def load():
    if not os.path.exists(PATH):
        return []
    with open(PATH) as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def save(notes):
    with open(PATH, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(notes, fh, indent=2)


def add(text, tags=None):
    notes = load()
    notes.append({"id": len(notes) + 1, "text": text, "tags": tags or []})
    save(notes)
    return notes[-1]

### Spec compliance

1. `notekeep/export.py:5-8`: `export_markdown(notes, path)` writes one `- text` bullet per note and returns the count, as the brief asks. It has no extra parameters or features and uses only the stdlib.

3. Scope check: `git diff e41ede0 -- notekeep/export.py tests/test_export.py` shows changes to the two named files only. Nothing is missing or extra, and nothing in the brief was misread.

⚠️ Cannot verify from diff:
1. The RED/GREEN runs in the report ("2 failed" → "2 passed", full suite "6 passed"). I did not re-run the suite, as instructed. The reported output shows no noise.
2. Whether non-ASCII text actually crashes on this machine. My one focused check (import `export_markdown` and export a note with non-ASCII text under the default encoding) was blocked when Bash permission was denied. Issue 1 below rests on reading the code, not on an observed run.

### Strengths
1. The implementation is 4 lines and matches the `with open(...) as fh` style in `store.py`.
2. The first test compares the whole file content exactly. A wrong separator, a missing newline or a missing prefix would all fail it.
3. The empty-list case is tested for both the return value (0) and the file content (empty).
4. The test data uses the real note shape (`id`, `text`, `tags`), matching `store.add`.

### Issues

#### Critical
None.

#### Important
1. `notekeep/export.py:5`: `open(path, "w")` uses the locale encoding. The report's risk 2 says this is "the same as store.py", but that is not correct:
   - `store.py` writes through `json.dump(...)`, which by default escapes every non-ASCII character. So `store.py` only ever writes ASCII, and its encoding never matters.
   - `export_markdown` writes the raw note text. On Windows (cp1252 by default), a note containing an emoji or a CJK character should raise `UnicodeEncodeError` partway through the loop, leaving a half-written file. Text like "café" would be written as cp1252 bytes rather than UTF-8 markdown.
   - Notes created through `store.add` can hold any text, so this defect is reachable on the platform the project is used on.
   - Fix: `open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8")`.

#### Minor
1. `tests/test_export.py:11,17`: `path.read_text()` also reads with the locale encoding, so the tests would not catch issue 1 even with non-ASCII data. Add a non-ASCII note and use `read_text(encoding="utf-8")`.
2. `notekeep/export.py:5`: an existing file at `path` is silently overwritten (mode `"w"`), and no test covers it. The report says so openly and it is a reasonable default. Coverage only.
3. Report risk 1 (no header, trailing newline, empty file when there are no notes): these follow directly from the brief's "one `- text` bullet each". This is not a finding.

### Assessment
**Task quality:** Needs fixes

**Reasoning:** The function meets the brief and the tests check real output. However, the implementer's reason for the default encoding is wrong: `store.py` only writes escaped ASCII, while export writes raw text. Exporting non-ASCII notes on Windows should therefore crash or produce a non-UTF-8 file. The fix is one argument, `encoding="utf-8"`, plus a non-ASCII test.

"""Notes on disk, one JSON file. Deliberately boring. No stage touches this."""
import json
import os

PATH = os.environ.get("NOTEKEEP_PATH", "notes.json")


def load():
    if not os.path.exists(PATH):
        return []
    with open(PATH) as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def save(notes):
    with open(PATH, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(notes, fh, indent=2)


def add(text, tags=None):
    notes = load()
    notes.append({"id": len(notes) + 1, "text": text, "tags": tags or []})
    save(notes)
    return notes[-1]

import json

from notekeep.as_json import to_json


def test_to_json_round_trips_and_is_indented():
    notes = [{"id": 1, "text": "buy milk", "tags": ["home"]}]
    out = to_json(notes)
    assert json.loads(out) == notes
    assert "\n  " in out
from notekeep.tags import with_tag


def test_with_tag_keeps_matching_notes_in_order():
    notes = [
        {"id": 1, "text": "a", "tags": ["work"]},
        {"id": 2, "text": "b", "tags": ["home"]},
        {"id": 3, "text": "c", "tags": ["home", "work"]},
    ]
    assert [n["id"] for n in with_tag(notes, "work")] == [1, 3]


def test_note_without_tags_key_matches_nothing():
    notes = [{"id": 1, "text": "a"}, {"id": 2, "text": "b", "tags": ["work"]}]
    assert [n["id"] for n in with_tag(notes, "work")] == [2]
from notekeep.export import export_markdown


def test_export_writes_one_bullet_per_note(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "notes.md"
    notes = [
        {"id": 1, "text": "buy milk", "tags": []},
        {"id": 2, "text": "call mum", "tags": ["family"]},
    ]
    assert export_markdown(notes, str(path)) == 2
    assert path.read_text() == "- buy milk\n- call mum\n"


def test_export_writes_utf8(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "notes.md"

"""Notes on disk, one JSON file. Deliberately boring. No stage touches this."""
import json
import os

PATH = os.environ.get("NOTEKEEP_PATH", "notes.json")


def load():
    if not os.path.exists(PATH):
        return []
    with open(PATH) as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def save(notes):
    with open(PATH, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(notes, fh, indent=2)


def add(text, tags=None):
    notes = load()
    notes.append({"id": len(notes) + 1, "text": text, "tags": tags or []})
    save(notes)
    return notes[-1]

"""Notes on disk, one JSON file. Deliberately boring. No stage touches this."""
import json
import os

PATH = os.environ.get("NOTEKEEP_PATH", "notes.json")


def load():
    if not os.path.exists(PATH):
        return []
    with open(PATH) as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def save(notes):
    with open(PATH, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(notes, fh, indent=2)


def add(text, tags=None):
    notes = load()
    notes.append({"id": len(notes) + 1, "text": text, "tags": tags or []})
    save(notes)
    return notes[-1]

**Critical** — none.

**Important** — none.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Reasoning:** All four stages match the plan, stay within their file boundaries, are tested against real behaviour, and every README claim is backed by the code; the remaining items are consistency nits and design-level choices with no functional impact.

All four stages are implemented and the full suite passes (7 tests). A final review of the whole branch approved it with no critical or important issues. **None of it is committed**: `git add` and `git commit` were blocked by permissions in this session, so everything is uncommitted changes in the working tree.

### Stages 1–3 (run in parallel; I checked first that they really touch separate files)
| Ref | Sub-feature | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | `to_json` + test | ✅ Done | Review approved. Output is indented 2 spaces, the same as `store.save`. |
| 2.1 | `with_tag` + tests for both cases | ✅ Done | Review approved. Keeps note order; a note with no `tags` key matches nothing. |
| 3.1 | `export_markdown` + tests | ✅ Done | The review found the file was written in the Windows default encoding, so notes with emoji or CJK text crashed. One fix round added `encoding="utf-8"` and a test that failed before the fix and passes after it. |

### Stage 4 (ran after 1–3)
| Ref | Sub-feature | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | README documents the three functions | 🔁 Done (modified approach) | **Why:** the agent that wrote it couldn't run anything, and a separate review of a 17-line doc change seemed like overkill. I ran every README snippet myself in a temp folder, outside the repo, and they all behave as documented. The final review checked each README claim against the code. **Effect:** stage 4 had one review instead of two. |

### How the run itself went
| Ref | Sub-feature | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | One commit per stage | ⏸ Deferred | **Why:** git write commands were blocked. **Effect:** the 7 changed files, plus the ticked `PLAN.md`, are uncommitted and you need to commit them. |
| 5.2 | Run log in `.skillator/run.md` | 🔁 Done (modified approach) | **Why:** running the run-log script was blocked. **Effect:** I kept the file by hand in the same format. It has every stage, every prompt sent and every decision I made. |
| 5.3 | Delete the per-stage `.taskwork/` folder at the end | ⏸ Deferred | **Why:** it holds the only test evidence for work that isn't committed. **Effect:** you can delete it once you've committed. |

**Score:** 4 ✅ · 2 🔁 · 2 ⏸ · 0 ❌. The three workarounds above (5.1, 5.2, 5.3) and two agents losing shell access all come from one cause: permissions in this session. Allowing `git` and `python` would remove them next time.

Decisions I made without asking:
1. `PLAN.md` had no task sections or project rules for the helper script to extract, so I wrote each stage's brief straight from its plan line. The only rules I gave the agents were the plan's own ("touch only the named files", "tests pass") plus "standard library only, keep it minimal".
2. Because stages 1–3 ran in the same folder at once, I told those agents not to commit, so I could commit each stage separately. In the end nothing could be committed (5.1).
3. Small review points I left open (logged in `run.md`):
   - `to_json` escapes non-ASCII characters, e.g. `café` becomes `caf\u00e9`, the same as `store.save`.
   - `with_tag` crashes if `tags` is `None`, which `store.add` never writes.
   - `export_markdown` needs a list, not a generator.
   - Two export tests read the file without `encoding="utf-8"`.

To commit it all:
```
git add notekeep tests README.md PLAN.md
git commit -m "notekeep v2: to_json, with_tag, export_markdown, README"
```
